name: Vossmark Filtercap Daily Commuter
description:
A structured six-panel cap in charcoal ripstop polyblend with a matte-black stiffened brim. The fabric has a faint grid-weave texture that repels light rain and smog particulate passively. Embroidered on the left panel: a small orange Vossmark transit-line logo, worn soft from washing. Inside the crown, a thin activated-carbon filter layer sits removable and washable.

The rear strap is a standard plastic snap closure with a small notched channel cut to clear a standard neural port bump—low-profile, nothing fancy. Available in charcoal, slate, and rust-orange.
functionality: Passive particulate filtration via carbon-layer crown. Water-resistant outer shell. Neural-port notch at rear closure accommodates standard single-port hardware. Sweatband wicks moisture during active commutes.
what_it_says: You're practical, employed, and not interested in making a statement.
story_hooks: Vossmark only sells these at company commissaries — owning one outside the transit system raises quiet questions about how you got it.
A specific batch from late 2199 has a filter layer that doubles as a passive signal interceptor — someone added it on the factory floor.
Two witnesses at a Circuit-level labor dispute were wearing identical Vossmark caps — someone is coordinating, and the cap is the signal.
